brief: Morgan Stanley attributes the Sep 30-Nov 5 AI selloff (AI & Tech Diffusion -26.6% vs ACWI -3.7%) to multiple compression, not earnings cuts: across 91 names, FY2 EPS rose about 3 log points while P/E fell about 37, more than the entire decline. Of 94 constituents, 61 have reported since Sep 30 and their estimates rose (median +4.5%). The other 33 have not yet reported. Valuation resets vary by region: US and Europe fell to the bottom quintile of their post-2019 ranges, Japan de-rated most (82nd to 28th percentile) despite resilient earnings, and Asia/EM stayed near its own median with the most downgrades. A hypothetical 20% EPS cut would push 55% of members above their own median P/E, versus 27% now, with cushions deepest in the US (24%) and thinnest in Japan (16%). Asia/EM is above its median. AI Adopters have outperformed Enablers by 26 points since Sep 30, but Enablers retain stronger earnings revisions (+48% net breadth vs +2%), so the rotation is valuation-led, not earnings-led. Capex-heavy reporters that raised capex estimates underperformed peers despite larger EPS upgrades, consistent with investors discounting capex-driven earnings. MS favours reducing upstream concentration, selective Adopter exposure, and regional valuation cushions over broad dip-buying.
